userStories.title: Plan the 10 Most Extraordinary Treehouses in America
userStories.description: Create a content plan for the treehouse roundup post. Target queries: 'best treehouse rentals USA', 'extraordinary treehouses America', 'treehouse Airbnb vacation', 'unique treehouse stays'. Post should embed 10 stay cards from the directory and read as a first-person editorial dispatch — not a numbered listicle, but a curated journey across American landscapes.
acceptanceCriteria: Target keyword identified
10 treehouse stays selected with geographic diversity
Post structure outlined (opening dispatch, stay sections organized by region/mood, closing tip)
Stay slugs to embed identified from the directory
Word count target set (1800-2500 words for 10 stays)
Meta title and meta description drafted
userStories.notes: Sprint 2 complete. 10 stays selected across 8 states, 4 regions.

userStories.title: Write first draft of extraordinary treehouses dispatch
userStories.description: Write the full editorial post. First-person voice. Warm, slightly literary. Not a numbered listicle — it reads like a letter from someone who spent a year sleeping in trees across America. Opens with scene-setting prose about the primal appeal of sleeping in a treehouse, then journeys through 10 stays. Organize by a narrative arc (maybe by geography or by the feeling each stay creates). Ends with a practical section.
acceptanceCriteria: Opening paragraph: atmospheric, sensory — why treehouses? the primal pull
10 stay recommendations woven into a narrative journey
Each stay: name, 2-3 sentences of editorial description, one detail that makes it extraordinary
Closing section: practical 'How to Choose Your Treehouse' tip
SEO keywords naturally integrated
Saved to content/drafts/extraordinary-treehouses-america.md

userStories.title: Review and sharpen the extraordinary treehouses draft
userStories.description: Self-review the draft. Strengthen the opening. Cut any generic travel writing cliches. Make sure each stay description earns its place and feels distinct (no two descriptions should sound alike). Add a compelling title and subtitle. Add meta description.
acceptanceCriteria: Opening paragraph revised to be more vivid/specific
Any cliches removed ('hidden gem', 'off the beaten path', 'like something out of a fairy tale', etc.)
Title: specific + searchable + editorial
Subtitle: evocative one-liner for the polaroid caption
Meta title: under 60 chars, includes 'Treehouse'
Meta description: under 160 chars, includes primary keyword
Each of the 10 stay descriptions feels distinct in voice and detail
Version 2 saved to content/drafts/extraordinary-treehouses-america-v2.md
userStories.notes: Sprint 2 complete. Cut cliches, fixed grammar, varied structures.
